transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-22
Start: 15:02 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Hui (Redwood SE), Nina Patel (Deckard SRE), Omar Ruiz (Deckard Head of ML), Jae Kim (Deckard Security), Marcus Lee (Deckard Platform)

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. We'll do a quick intro and then Marcus is going to drive the console flow.
[00:06] Nina Patel: Hi all, thanks, yeah we got our calendar aligned. We want to focus on the failure cases and how fast our oncall can triage from the UI.
[00:12] Marcus Hui: Great, I will share my screen, uh -- just let me know if the resolution looks off.
[00:18] Omar Ruiz: We sent two sample prompt sets earlier, hope that helps to do a realistic replay.
[00:23] Marcus Hui: Yep I have those. Okay pulling up Redwood Console -> Requests -> Inspector view.
[00:28] [screen share noise] 
[00:31] Marcus Hui: So the inspector is centered around request journeys: you get the request metadata, token timing, model variant used, KV-cache hits, and the trace that links back to the serving runtime.
[00:42] Jae Kim: Quick Q: can we see who accessed the request historically? audit logs?
[00:46] Marcus Hui: Yes, in the top-right there's an audit trail link; it shows token-level actions and API keys used, we can pivot to the audit logs page.
[00:52] [00:52] Nina Patel: And retention on those logs? We've got to keep them for 13 months for our compliance posture.
[00:58] Lena Park: For Dedicated and Private plans we have extended retention add-ons, can store up to 18 months, and you can point to your own S3 with lifecycle rules, also KMS in front.
[01:10] Nina Patel: K, good.
[01:12] Marcus Hui: Back to the request, here's an example failed request -- status code 503 from the model node. You can see latency timeline: client -> gateway -> model -> fallback.
[01:22] [01:22] Marcus Hui: The trace shows a KV miss at token 32, then a fallback to cold-start quantized variant at token 47; you'll see the perf spike there.
[01:32] Omar Ruiz: Wait, uh -- cold-start? We were expecting warm KV cache for most sessions in prod.
[01:37] Marcus Hui: Right, so this trace suggests the prefix wasn't cached; possible causes: the routing policy routed to a different hardware pool, or the cached KV shard had evicted.
[01:46] Nina Patel: How do we tell eviction vs new routing?
[01:49] Marcus Hui: There's a KV cache diagnostics tab on the same request inspector. It shows eviction events and shard IDs. See here, eviction at 14:03:12 UTC with a reason 'mem-pressure-evict'.
[01:59] Nina Patel: Hmm, mem-pressure-evict. We're seeing that in our telemetry spikes during batch windows.
[02:05] Marcus Hui: If you pin this model variant or increase cache quota per instance, the eviction rate drops; Redwood Optimize can recommend a cache profile based on sequence length distribution.
[02:15] Lena Park: Also note routing policies, you can set preference for warm nodes, or a fallback to a less-quantized variant to avoid cold-start perf spikes.
[02:24] [02:24] Omar Ruiz: What's the tradeoff for pinning? more cost?
[02:28] Marcus Hui: Yes pinning consumes reserved capacity on Dedicated, or increases buffer allocations on Hosted. Unit cost rises but latency improves and less variance.
[02:36] Jae Kim: Security question: when a request fails and we export traces to our S3, do we redact PII automatically?
[02:42] Marcus Hui: There's a built-in redaction step in the export flow; default redaction filters for emails, credit-card-ish patterns, but you can add custom regex in Private deployments.
[02:52] Jae Kim: Good, will need that written down for our audit.
[02:55] 
[03:00] Marcus Hui: I'm going to demonstrate trace playback now. Playback replays the token timeline and overlays model metrics per token.
[03:07] [03:07] Marcus Hui: (plays) you can scrub to token 40 — see latency jump from 18ms to 180ms. That lines up with the fallback.
[03:16] Nina Patel: Could that 180ms be network hop to different region?
[03:19] Marcus Hui: It can; this trace shows region is the same, so it's internal runtime switch. The trace object includes region, instance id, and model binary hash so you can correlate.
[03:30] Omar Ruiz: Model binary hash? We're using pinned hashes in our deployment, yes?
[03:34] Marcus Hui: If you pin the model version in your rollout policy you get invariant model hashes; the console shows mismatches.
[03:40] [03:40] Marcus Lee: I want to dig into the error classifier you mentioned earlier. How are errors labeled? 503 vs user error?
[03:46] Marcus Hui: We have an error classifier that groups errors into service, model, and client categories. It uses heuristics + optional user tags. For instance this 503 had a service-level precondition: insufficient KV availability.
[03:57] Nina Patel: Can we add a custom rule so a particular prompt triggers a 'sensitive' label?
[04:02] Marcus Hui: Yes there's a rules engine in Optimize — you can tag requests by regex or by scored evals. Those tagged requests feed into alerts and different retention buckets.
[04:12] Lena Park: Quick interjection — we've seen customers using that to route high-risk traffic to Private clusters.
[04:18] Omar Ruiz: That is interesting. Okay continue.
[04:21] [04:21] Marcus Hui: Showing the request timeline combined with the SLO panel — here's a 99th pct token latency heatmap. You can filter by model variant, route, and customer key.
[04:33] Nina Patel: For our SLOs we measure 95th token latency per customer key per day. Can we export daily aggregates?
[04:39] Marcus Hui: Yes exports available, plus an API endpoint to pull SLO metrics. We'll add export examples to the follow-up note.
[04:46] [04:46] Omar Ruiz: On the topic of reproductions — you mentioned a replay sandbox earlier?
[04:50] Marcus Hui: Correct. There's a replay sandbox where you can replay historic requests against different model variants or quantization profiles without affecting production; it's isolated and uses synthetic keys.
[04:59] Jae Kim: Do those runs stay in Redwood? We want to ensure they aren't stored longer than necessary.
[05:03] Marcus Hui: Replays have a short retention by default and can be auto-deleted. In Private, you host the sandbox.
[05:10] Nina Patel: Okay that covers traces + playback. I want to see how a multi-request journey surfaces — like a chat session with context windows.
[05:16] Marcus Hui: Sure. Here's a session view: you get per-message request nodes and a session KV map. You can expand any node to see the KV snapshot at that time.
[05:26] [05:26] Marcus Hui: E.g., message 4 shows a mismatch in the user system token count vs actual. That explains why the model truncated.
[05:33] Omar Ruiz: Truncate? We see occasional hallucinated completions when tokens are dropped.
[05:37] Marcus Hui: Right, token mismatch -> wrong context -> degraded output. The console surfaces warnings when token windows exceed the configured sequence length.
[05:45] Nina Patel: Do we get alerting for that? We need a Slack channel when token-overflow occurs.
[05:49] Marcus Hui: Yes, you can set alerts in Console to post to Slack, PagerDuty, or the Redwood webhook.
[05:55] [05:55] Lena Park: Quick question from me — have you benchmarked with long sequences? In your email you mentioned bursty long contexts.
[06:02] Omar Ruiz: We see spikes to 8k tokens during customer sessions, yes.
[06:06] Marcus Hui: For 8k we suggest quantized LLM variants with chunked KV handling. Optimize will recommend a quantization profile and a batching policy to reduce tokens per call.
[06:15] Jae Kim: And encryption at rest for those KV shards?
[06:18] Marcus Hui: Yes we support KMS-backed encryption both on Hosted (Redwood-managed KMS) and Private (customer-managed KMS/HSM).
[06:25] Nina Patel: Good. Also can you show an example of a canary deploy rollback in the Console?
[06:30] Marcus Hui: Sure — in the Rollouts tab you can pick a canary, view per-variant error rates and latency, and either promote or rollback.
[06:37] [06:37] Marcus Hui: Here's a demo canary where a variant had a 4x error rate at 99th pct; you can set auto-rollback thresholds.
[06:44] Omar Ruiz: Auto-rollback to what? Previous variant or fallback?
[06:47] Marcus Hui: You can configure both: automatic fallback to a compatible variant or roll back the new variant entirely.
[06:53] [06:53] Nina Patel: We need a policy in our runbook to pick one over the other.
[06:57] Lena Park: We can share a playbook example. We'll include a runbook template in the follow-up.
[07:02] [07:02] Marcus Hui: Alright I'm going to intentionally trigger the KV miss in a sandbox to show the end-to-end debug flow.
[07:08] [07:08] Nina Patel: Perfect.
[07:09] [07:09] Marcus Hui: (typing) executing synthetic request... now — see the inspector flagged a 'kv-eviction' and created an auto-ticket with a prefilled link to the trace and suggested remediation steps.
[07:21] Omar Ruiz: Auto-ticket? Where does that go?
[07:24] Marcus Hui: It can create issues in JIRA, or Slack threads, or attach directly to your SRE dashboard via webhook.
[07:30] Marcus Lee: We use JIRA; can we map Redwood tickets to our project and template?
[07:34] Marcus Hui: Yes Jira integration supports mapping fields, templates, and automations. We'll include config notes.
[07:40] [07:40] Nina Patel: We noticed in one of our incidents the trace IDs didn't line up with our logs. How do we correlate?
[07:46] Marcus Hui: Request Inspector includes a correlation id and supports custom headers. If you inject your request-id into the Redwood request header, it appears in the trace and audit logs.
[07:57] Jae Kim: Our security team will want signed trace exports — can Redwood sign exported traces or provide chain-of-custody metadata?
[08:03] Marcus Hui: We provide attestations: export manifest, SHA hashes of artifacts, and per-export audit entries. In Private deployments we can integrate with your signing HSM.
[08:14] Lena Park: Okay want to open up for specific Deckard questions.
[08:18] Nina Patel: For the benchmark Marcus will run, can we specify our normal traffic shape and paste the sample vectors we sent earlier?
[08:24] Marcus Hui: Absolutely. If you give us the vectors, we'll run the bench under your traffic mix and share the KV hit/miss heatmaps.
[08:30] Omar Ruiz: One last question — pricing for Dedicated buffer to avoid KV eviction, is it flat or per-instance?
[08:36] Lena Park: It's usually per-reserved-instance with optional burst credits. I'll send the sheet with two configurations: pinned pool vs autoscaled with high-memory instances.
[08:46] [08:46] Marcus Hui: Wrapping up — recap: 1) We'll run a KV-cache fallback benchmark with Deckard vectors, 2) Lena will send pricing and SSO docs, 3) Deckard will upload anonymized traces.
[08:56] Nina Patel: Sounds good. Please include the playbook template and the redaction regex examples.
[09:03] Lena Park: Will do. One more note — competitors sometimes tout simpler UIs but lack request-level traceplayback; happy to show a deeper walkthrough if you want a larger workshop.
[09:12] Omar Ruiz: We might want a 2-hr workshop for the SRE+Sec team.
[09:16] Lena Park: Great, we'll propose dates. Thanks everyone.
[09:20] [09:20] Meeting ends.

Notes on transcription: occasional audio dropouts at 00:28 and 07:08; some product names transcribed as "request inspector" vs "request inspector" interchangeably; minor mis-hearings ("KV cash" instead of "KV cache") are present.
